class.name: TriangleMesh
class.brief_description: Triangle geometry for efficient, physicsless intersection queries.
class.description: Creates a bounding volume hierarchy (BVH) tree structure around triangle geometry. The triangle BVH tree can be used for efficient intersection queries without involving a physics engine. For example, this can be used in editor tools to select objects with complex shapes based on the mouse cursor position. [b]Performance:[/b] Creating the BVH tree for complex geometry is a slow process and best done in a background thread.

method.name: create_from_faces
method.description: Creates the BVH tree from an array of faces. Each 3 vertices of the input [param faces] array represent one triangle (face). Returns [code]true[/code] if the tree is successfully built, [code]false[/code] otherwise.

method.name: update_from_indexed_surfaces
method.description: Builds or refits directly from paired arrays of indexed triangle surfaces, without creating a rendering mesh. Each vertex entry must be a [PackedVector3Array] and each index entry a [PackedInt32Array] with a multiple of three indices. An empty index array contributes no faces; non-indexed input requires explicit sequential indices. Faces are concatenated in surface order. As with [method create_from_faces], a new build uses surface index zero for every face. Returns [code]false[/code] without modifying the existing tree for mismatched array lengths, wrong entry types, invalid indices, non-finite referenced positions, or zero total faces. If [param refit] is [code]true[/code], also requires an existing tree and unchanged total face count, with the same limitations as [method refit_from_faces]. Callers must rebuild rather than refit when semantic topology or face ordering changes.

method.name: refit_from_faces
method.description: Updates an existing tree's triangle positions and bounds without rebuilding its partition. The input must contain the same number of vertices as the previous build, in the same face order. Returns [code]false[/code] without modifying the tree if it is not valid, the count differs, or any input coordinate is non-finite. Uses the same coordinate snapping and face-normal calculation as [method create_from_faces]. Corners welded by the original build may separate; refitted geometry stores independent corners, which may use more vertex memory. Face and surface indices retain their original ordering. For equal-distance hits on overlapping faces or shared edges, the winning face may differ from a freshly rebuilt partition. Repeated or large deformations may reduce query performance because the partition is retained. Rebuild periodically or when profiling indicates degraded traversal. Do not update and query the same instance concurrently.

method.name: get_faces
method.description: Returns a copy of the geometry faces. Each 3 vertices of the array represent one triangle (face).

method.name: intersect_ray
method.description: Tests for intersection with a ray starting at [param begin] and facing [param dir] and extending toward infinity. If an intersection with a triangle happens, returns a [Dictionary] with the following fields: [code]position[/code]: The position on the intersected triangle. [code]normal[/code]: The normal of the intersected triangle. [code]face_index[/code]: The index of the intersected triangle. Returns an empty [Dictionary] if no intersection happens. See also [method intersect_segment], which is similar but uses a finite-length segment.

method.name: intersect_segment
method.description: Tests for intersection with a segment going from [param begin] to [param end]. If an intersection with a triangle happens returns a [Dictionary] with the following fields: [code]position[/code]: The position on the intersected triangle. [code]normal[/code]: The normal of the intersected triangle. [code]face_index[/code]: The index of the intersected triangle. Returns an empty [Dictionary] if no intersection happens. See also [method intersect_ray], which is similar but uses an infinite-length ray.
